text:
Maya: Heads-up: after landing the prefetch/warmup change we see a regression with AWQ Mixtral setups on longer sequences. p95 latency up ~18% on our perf harness.
Sam: Can you paste the perf numbers and configs? model, sequence, batch, quantization profile?
Maya: numbers from nightly run: model=mixtral-8x7-awq, kernel=optimized-fwd-v2, rope_scale=1.0, batch=1, seq=2048. p50=78ms, p95=210ms (was 178ms last week), tokens/s down from 850 -> 720 on same hardware.
Eli: interesting. is this only AWQ or do GPTQ/INT8 runs also change?
Maya: quick checks: gptq baseline (same build) p95=182ms, INT8 (generic) p95=188ms — so AWQ seems worst hit.
Noor: any KV cache miss stats? warmup change touched prefetch + KV eviction timing.
Maya: KV hit rate printed by harness: before=99.1%, after=97.4% for long sequences (we warmup 512 tokens then continue). KV miss spikes around boundary when we switch warmup->steady batching.
Sam: could be batcher steering changed the kernel selection mid-request; kernel switch causes extra memcpy/transpose overhead.
Maya: stack trace from trace logs (trimmed):

```
[perf] kernel_select: selected optimized-fwd-v2 for seq<=512
[perf] runtime: patching kernel->fallback-gemm for seq>512 during stream
[latency] memcpy: 12.3ms
```

Eli: that fallback path is expensive. Why did it pick optimized-fwd-v2 initially if it needs fallback later? kernel selection policy should pick a single kernel for request lifetime.
Noor: we recently introduced dynamic kernel steering where the kernel decision can change when the KV layout transitions (to support prefetched KV packing). looks like it flips for certain RoPE scaled runs.
Maya: config snippet for the failing run:

```
model: mixtral-8x7
quant: awq
rope_scale: 1.0
prefetch: true
warmup_tokens: 512
batching: dynamic
kernel_policy: latency-first
```

Sam: Do we have a repro script? Can we run microbench that logs kernel decisions per token index?
Maya: added a small harness: ./tools/bench_kv_prefetch --model mixtral-8x7 --quant awq --seq 2048 --warmup 512 --log-kernel. output shows kernel flip at token 513 consistently.
Eli: hypothesis: RoPE scaling + AWQ quant layout changes the KV stride so optimized-fwd-v2 is invalid past some seq and runtime inserts fallback instead of choosing fallback up front.
Noor: check kernel compatibility table: optimized-fwd-v2 does not support packed-KV stride > 64 for our AWQ layout.
Sam: That explains the memcpy: when kernel flips it needs to repack KV which is expensive mid-request.
Maya: two questions: 1) can we update kernel selection to be conservative and pick fallback up front when prefetch/warmup indicates future stride change; 2) does GPTQ have same layout issue?
Eli: GPTQ layout keeps stride <=64 so it didn't flip. AWQ's packer currently uses 80-byte stride in this model due to per-head quant params.
Noor: proposal: add a preflight check during kernel selection that simulates resulting KV stride after warmup and picks compatible kernel for entire request.
Sam: good. also we can add a fast-path in the packer to avoid repack mid-request: when kernel flips, do in-place convert without full memcpy if layout difference is simple.
Maya: action items:
- Noor: prototype preflight kernel-selection check (PR)
- Sam: small packer in-place convert (opt)
- Eli: add microbench to perf harness that logs kernel id per token and KV copy times
- Maya: run cross-quant suite (AWQ vs GPTQ vs INT8 vs FP8) over 2d grid (rope_scale x warmup)

Noor: I'll open PR with tests using the bench_kv_prefetch harness. target PR by EOD tomorrow.
Sam: I'll sketch in-place convert and bench it. If in-place reduces memcpy from 12ms -> <2ms we're good.
Eli: for calibration prompts: we should ensure AWQ calibration doesn't add per-head tails that change stride. Maya, can you attach the calib prompts you used?
Maya: attaching sample prompts (copied inline):

"""
calib_prompt_A: "Summarize the following in one sentence: <long legal doc>",
calib_prompt_B: "Translate the paragraph to Spanish: <tech manual excerpt>",
calib_prompt_C: "Answer open-ended: what are the steps to refactor a monolith to services?"
"""

Noor: If calib prompts have variable tokenization per head they can change per-head scaling metadata. I'll run calib again forcing uniform chunks.
Sam: Also run a quick AB: AWQ w/pack_stride_forced=64 vs default.
Maya: running now on dedicated node, will post numbers when done.
infra-bot: nightly-perf-run: job 47123 started on node gpu-c-07.
Maya: AB results (short): AWQ default p95=210ms, AWQ forced-stride64 p95=186ms, GPTQ p95=182ms.
Eli: that aligns with hypothesis. forcing stride avoids fallback.
Noor: conclusion: AWQ packer defaults can create strides incompatible with some kernels. when combined with prefetch/warmup kernel steering it causes mid-request repack and latency regression.
Maya: decision: short-term -> add preflight check and add forced-stride config for AWQ profiles in catalog; medium-term -> update AWQ packer to prefer stride<=64 when kernel pool contains non-packed kernels.
Sam: I'll file follow-up infra task to backfill regression tests into CI perf suite.
Maya: Thanks team. I'll keep thread updated with PR links and perf runs.
infra-bot: job 47123 completed: summary attached to /perf/runs/47123.
Noor: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/rt-runtime/pull/582 (preflight check + tests).
Sam: PR for in-place convert WIP at https://github.com/redwood/rt-runtime/pull/589.
Maya: closing loop: after PR merged AWQ p95 improved to 189ms on the harness; still 3-4% worse than GPTQ but acceptable given AWQ accuracy tradeoffs.
Eli: let's also add a note in model catalog: AWQ mixtral-8x7 default profile = forced-stride64 for now.
Maya: done. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
